question: Can PAREX revised EIS station FWE 6 be assigned to a named river, channel, floodway, or lake using independent source-named waterway evidence?
method: Compared the exact PAREX FWE 6 DMS coordinate against the official EIS map metadata, a single WGS84 Nominatim reverse-geocode response, and the waterway names in the official EMB-hosted 2023 revised-draft MRT4 EIS. Nominatim was called once, with a named User-Agent, and its response retained locally with SHA-256. Its nearest-object result is treated only as an OSM discovery clue, not as a waterway or legal administrative determination.

station.waterbodyContextAsPrinted: Table 2-16 is captioned as freshwater ecology sampling sites along the Pasig River; the source separately labels FWE 6 locality as Taytay, Rizal. Figure 2-51 shows the southeastern project end but does not identify the exact channel or lake at FWE 6.
station.sourceCoordinateDatum: Figure 2-51 states WGS 1984, but the report does not explicitly state that the Table 2-16 coordinate pair uses that datum; WGS84 was used only as a provisional input for one exploratory lookup.

independentWaterwayContext.locator: Revised Draft EIS, May 2023, Section 3.2.1 Hydrology/Hydrogeology, page ES-12; lines/source text describe Taytay drainage context.
waterwayNamesAsPrinted: Antipolo River (present course of Manggahan Floodway)
reportedRelationships: The report says Taytay River, Hulo River, and Napindan Channel empty into Laguna Lake.
It says Taytay River joins the Antipolo River (present course of Manggahan Floodway) near barangays Sta. Ana and San Juan.
independentWaterwayContext.coordinateToWaterwayLink: No PAREX FWE 6 point, matching station ID, or coordinate-to-waterway linkage appears in this MRT4 EIS passage. The named systems are candidate context only.

mapCrossCheck.returnedAddressAsPrinted: C-6 Extension bike lane, Purok 8, Santa Ana, Pasig Second District, Pasig, Eastern Manila District, Rizal, Metro Manila, 1920, Philippines
mapCrossCheck.resultInterpretation: The nearest suitable indexed OSM object is a road feature tagged as a cycleway (“C-6 Extension bike lane”), with an OSM address label for Santa Ana/Pasig. It is not a waterway object. Reverse-geocoding snaps to a suitable indexed object and does not assert that the sampling happened on that road or settle the official station municipality.

decision.disposition: Keep FWE 6 attached to the source’s reported Taytay locality and Pasig-corridor EIS context, but flag the coordinate/locality crosswalk as unresolved. The OSM result does not override the source label and does not identify the waterbody.

limitations: A one-day environmental-survey station coordinate is not a fishing spot or waterbody boundary.

The PAREX report’s municipality label and the OSM reverse-geocoder address result differ; Nominatim documentation explicitly says it returns the closest suitable indexed OSM object and can return a different street or unexpected address.
The MRT4 EIS provides municipality-level waterway names and general drainage relationships, not an FWE 6 coordinate crosswalk.
No authoritative coordinate geometry, field notebook, corrected survey table, station photographs, fish voucher, or site-specific license evidence was established here.
The source’s separate 14-species narrative versus 13-binomial tables and Table 2-19/Table 2-20 name conflicts remain unchanged and outside this locality-only review.
nextActions: Keep FWE 6 and its fish names research-only; do not transfer it to the named Taytay channels or Laguna de Bay.

Use a source-matched field coordinate record or a clearly labeled station map with waterway label as the minimum independent resolution evidence; do not infer from nearest streets or municipal name alone.
Continue the NCR waterbody evidence inventory using independently source-named, site-resolved datasets.
